**Finding: AUDIT — compliant (no redline proposed).**

The agreement contains no audit right against Sparkling. Targeted searches (audit, inspection, verification, records, monitoring, remote access, certification/usage reporting, right to enter/examine, business-hours access) returned no responsive clause, and I read every plausible location in full:

- **§3 Restrictions on Use (p0029–p0037, plus (g) at p0039)** — imposes copy/reverse-engineering/service-bureau restrictions on Sparkling but attaches **no verification or inspection mechanic** to police them.
- **§10 Maintenance and Support (p0064–p0073)** — the only access right runs the other way (Sparkling's telephone access to Garman personnel); no Garman remote or on-site access to our systems.
- **§14 Confidentiality (p0094–p0101)** — references "accounting records" only in the definition of Confidential Information, not as an inspection right.
- **§20 / Page 10 general matters (p0134–p0147)** — notices, waiver, assignment, force majeure, severability, governing law; no audit provision.

Because there is no audit right binding Customer at all, there is no frequency, notice, cost-allocation or system-access exposure to constrain. This sits above the preferred position (which only limits an existing audit right), so it is not a "missing" clause in a way that harms us — inserting audit machinery to satisfy the checklist elements would manufacture a Vendor right we have not granted and weaken our position. No redline proposed.
